Does a slashed validator skip the exit queue? **Context of this question:** When a validator is slashed, it gets 3 types of penalty: - Initial penalty (`1/32` of effective balance, let's say 1ETH) - Leak during `~36 days`, let's say `0.08 ETH` cumulated penalty during these 36 days - A correlation penalty at `~18 days` depending of how many other validators are slashed in a window of `~36 days` center around the validator slashing epoch. (Let's say `0 ETH` since we need `> 1%` of total validators to be be slashed for this penalty to be `> 0 ETH`). Let's imagine the exit queue is very long (several months). If a slashed validator skips the exit queue, it could be, in some circumstances, interesting to lose "only" `~1.08 ETH` (+ maybe correlation penalty) and to wait "only" for 36 days than losing no ETH at all and wait for several months before being able to withdraw. Doesn't `slash_validator` just call `initiate_validator_exit`? So no skipping of queue afaict ( <@531934490826768418> ) https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#slash_validator So if I understand correctly, a slashed validator leaks during `~36 days` + during the whole time it is in the exit queue? Not exactly. A slashed validator gets penalties applied until its withdrawable epoch. As you can see in that function I linked, that's set to ```validator.withdrawable_epoch = max(validator.withdrawable_epoch, Epoch(epoch + EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR))``` So if the queue is _really_ long (like months), they'll also get penalties for that long. (At least from what I can tell, I didn't know/realize this either) See `get_eligible_validator_indices` , which is used for these penalty-applying-functions. Basically those functions will loop over all active validators, _and_ all slashed validators even if they are no longer active (until they can withdraw) OK super clear! Thanks for pointing out this line in the spec! Oh, thank you alot

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Does a slashed validator skip the exit queue?

**Context of this question:**

When a validator is slashed, it gets 3 types of penalty:
- Initial penalty (`1/32` of effective balance, let's say 1ETH)
- Leak during `~36 days`, let's say `0.08 ETH` cumulated penalty during these 36 days
- A correlation penalty at `~18 days` depending of how many other validators are slashed in a window of `~36 days` center around the validator slashing epoch. (Let's say `0 ETH` since we need `> 1%` of total validators to be be slashed for this penalty to be `> 0 ETH`).

Let's imagine the exit queue is very long (several months).
If a slashed validator skips the exit queue, it could be, in some circumstances, interesting to lose "only" `~1.08 ETH` (+ maybe correlation penalty) and to wait "only" for 36 days than losing no ETH at all and wait for several months before being able to withdraw.

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Doesn't `slash_validator` just call `initiate_validator_exit`? So no skipping of queue afaict ( <@531934490826768418> )

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: So if I understand correctly, a slashed validator leaks during `~36 days` + during the whole time it is in the exit queue?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Not exactly. A slashed validator gets penalties applied until its withdrawable epoch. As you can see in that function I linked, that's set to ```validator.withdrawable_epoch = max(validator.withdrawable_epoch, Epoch(epoch + EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR))```

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: So if the queue is _really_ long (like months), they'll also get penalties for that long.

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: (At least from what I can tell, I didn't know/realize this either)

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: See `get_eligible_validator_indices` , which is used for these penalty-applying-functions. Basically those functions will loop over all active validators, _and_ all slashed validators even if they are no longer active (until they can withdraw)
